clue.text: Bully put away after quarrel in B&B

indicators.note: the word for put away comes after the B&B construction
the quarrel word is placed inside the two letters of the bed-and-breakfast abbreviation

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, supplies two Bs
a quarrel is a row
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A guest-house owner bullies someone after a quarrel at the B&B.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them with stern looks and words, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Old soldiers pointing to sign

parts.note: soldiers are men, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Veteran troops pointing to a portent of what is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury is a sign of something to come, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Notice in job centre in Beverley

parts.note: a job is a post

indicators.note: the two letters at the very centre of the town name are taken

explanation.surface: A vacancy notice pinned up in the job centre in the Yorkshire town of Beverley.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice put up on a wall is a placard or bill, a printed sheet for display.

clue.text: Mean to consume mostly fresh fish

indicators.note: the word for mean swallows the shortened word, holding it inside

parts.note: mean, as in tight-fisted, is stingy

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fresh, uncooked food is raw

explanation.surface: A miser deciding to eat fish that is mostly fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray with a venomous barbed tail is a kind of flat fish.

clue.text: Colourful scholar entertaining lad in apartment

indicators.note: the whole construction goes inside the apartment word

parts.note: an apartment is a flat

indicators.note: the man word entertains, that is holds inside, the word for a lad

parts.note: as printed the word is meant to give the man word; the corrected clue reads bloke, and a bloke is a man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A colourful academic putting up a young man in their apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's slip: 'scholar' would be MA, leaving an unexplained N. The intended word was 'bloke', which the Telegraph website later substituted.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, exuberant and brightly ostentatious describes someone or something colourful in style.

clue.text: Collection round pub raised for sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole is read from the bottom up
the collection word goes round the pub word

parts.note: a collection of things is a set
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A whip-round collected at the pub to fund a sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket game played over a net is one sport among many, so this is an example.

clue.text: Instrument produced by gypsy chap cutting steak

indicators.note: the gypsy word cuts into the steak word, splitting it

parts.note: a T-bone is a cut of steak
a Rom is a Romany man

explanation.surface: A musical instrument conjured by a traveller slicing a steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gypsy chap' is a Romany man; a T-bone is a cut of steak.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument with a slide is a specific example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Fair play from English, somewhat reduced before close of play

indicators.note: the shortened word comes before the final letter
reduced means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: somewhat, as in fairly, is quite

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire seeing fair play as English batting slows before close of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' docks the final letter of the word for somewhat; the E at the front is English, not the letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice and impartial treatment are what fair play means, so the terms are synonyms.

clue.text: One who informs bank worker

definitions.meaning: someone who tells or relates things
a cashier serving customers at a bank counter

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb tell: one who tells a tale, and one who counts out money in a bank.

clue.text: Tense victory secures double

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A nervy win that clinches a double triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A double, someone exactly alike, is a counterpart or matching partner.

clue.text: What we're called during explosive competition

indicators.note: the phrase sits during, that is inside, the explosive

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
what we are called is our name

explanation.surface: Our name gets read out during a fiery, combustible contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of contests between players to find an overall winner is a competition.

clue.text: Sensitive offer

definitions.meaning: sore or easily hurt to the touch
to put forward formally, as with a bid or a resignation

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an adjective for sore or delicate and a verb or noun for a formal bid.

clue.text: Leave time to include guys in office

indicators.note: the leave-plus-time letters take the guys inside them

parts.note: to leave is to depart
guys are men

explanation.surface: Taking time off work to bring some colleagues into the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A government ministry or a division of an organisation is an office.

clue.text: Reptile in store — it desperately gulps oxygen

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gulp, swallowing the symbol for oxygen
acting desperately, the letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A creature kept in a shop, desperately gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles STORE and IT into TORTISE, which 'gulps' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow land animal with a domed shell is one kind of reptile.

clue.text: Two sons leaving corks for hat

indicators.note: the two letters leave, so they are removed

parts.note: corks are bottle stoppers
S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons give two Ss

explanation.surface: Two boys depart, leaving corks behind, in exchange for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last S of STOPPERS go.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat, the tall formal silk kind, is a hat.

clue.text: Working MO, deeply involved

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A modus operandi deeply bound up in the work.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is printed in capitals as if for modus operandi, but it is simply anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a job means working, so the adjective and participle are synonyms.

clue.text: Absolute ruler's angry tirade after Troy gutted

indicators.note: the tirade word comes after the gutted city
a gutted word has its insides removed, keeping only first and last letters

parts.note: an angry tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A despot rants furiously after the fall of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot with unlimited power is an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Very hot current across river

indicators.note: the current word is laid across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: current, as in topical news, is of present interest

explanation.surface: A sweltering current flowing across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The climate near the equator is sweltering, so very hot weather is so described.

clue.text: Court giving support to current policeman's charge

indicators.note: in a down clue the court letters sit below and so support the rest

parts.note: current, as in fashionable, is in
a DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: A court backing an officer's bid to bring charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' is the last piece, though it opens the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone of a crime is to charge them.

clue.text: Easy shot bagging stray animal

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the shot word holds the stray word

parts.note: a tap-in is an easy shot in football or golf
to stray is to err

explanation.surface: A sportsman's simple shot bagging a stray creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is a specific kind of animal.

clue.text: Faux pas made by troublesome children heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: naughty children are little terrors

explanation.surface: Social blunders committed by naughty kids as they head off.
explanation.definitionFit: Faux pas, a plural here, are social mistakes or blunders.

clue.text: Display tawdry items also

parts.note: tat is cheap and tawdry stuff
also means too

explanation.surface: Showing off cheap, gaudy trinkets as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A military display, such as the Edinburgh show of marching bands, is called this.

clue.text: The man taken in by Conservative's surmise

indicators.note: the man words are taken inside the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
the man is he

explanation.surface: A man fooled by a Conservative politician's speculation.
explanation.definitionFit: A surmise is a supposition or hypothesis, an idea not yet proven.

clue.text: Later on I worried about member's gymnastic apparatus

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, enclosing, the member
worried means fretted at and pulled around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone worries over a Member of Parliament's gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns LATER ON I into TRAOLINE, which goes 'about' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas sheet for bouncing on is a piece of gym equipment.

clue.text: Helpful hint involving end of pier ride

indicators.note: the hint word involves, enclosing, the letter

parts.note: a helpful hint is a tip

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A useful tip about the funfair ride at the end of the pier.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey or excursion is a ride or outing.

clue.text: Instant credit

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in just a second
buying on credit, as in on the slate

explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage gives one short word both for a moment and for buying on credit.

clue.text: Spell and sign name inside

indicators.note: the name letter goes inside the sign word

parts.note: a sign or slight indication is a trace

explanation.surface: A magic spell, a sign, and a name written inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell, as in being under one, is a hypnotic or dreamlike state.

clue.text: Go and film defector

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
a film is a thin coat or layer

explanation.surface: Go and see the film about a defector.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who switches sides is a renegade or traitor, the same as a defector.
